title: Measuring angles
keyIdea: Angles are measured in degrees (°) with a protractor. Put the protractor's centre mark on the vertex and line up its 0 line along one arm. A protractor has two scales, so read the one that starts at 0 on that arm, and count up to where the other arm crosses. Estimate first to check: an acute angle is less than 90°, an obtuse angle is between 90° and 180°. To draw an angle, mark the size on the same scale and join the mark to the vertex. A reflex angle is 360° minus the inside angle.
familyTip: Draw a few angles with a ruler, swap papers and measure each other's with a protractor. Say 'acute, so less than 90' or 'obtuse, so more than 90' out loud before reading, and check that the reading agrees.

visual.caption: Is each reading sensible, or was the wrong scale used? Drag each to a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: A narrow, pointy angle read as 160°

lab.caption: Flagship lab: line a protractor up on the vertex, pick the right scale, estimate before measuring, draw 135° and 70°, and measure reflex angles.

kid: We measure angles in degrees. A small circle after a number means degrees, like 47°. A protractor is the tool we use.
Put the small cross in the middle of the protractor on the vertex. That is the point where the two arms meet. Then lay the 0 line along one arm.
A protractor has two rows of numbers. Use the row that starts at 0 on your arm. Count up to where the other arm crosses.
Guess first. A sharp, pointy angle is less than 90°. A wide angle is more than 90°. If your reading does not match your guess, you read the wrong row.
adult: Ages 9 to 10. This is the Year 5 geometry objective in the National Curriculum in England. Children know angles are measured in degrees. They estimate and compare acute, obtuse and reflex angles. They draw given angles, and measure them in degrees (°). Key words: angle, degree, protractor, vertex, arm, baseline, inner scale, outer scale, acute, obtuse, right angle, reflex, estimate.

The two scales run in opposite directions. So any arm crosses two numbers that add to 180. The right one is on the scale whose 0 lies on the arm you lined up. To draw an angle, mark the size on that scale. Then join the mark to the vertex with a ruler. A half-circle protractor cannot read a reflex angle directly. Measure the inside angle and take it away from 360°.

Common mistakes: reading the wrong scale (47° read as 133°); putting the centre mark at the end of an arm or on the edge, not on the vertex; starting from the protractor's edge rather than the 0 line; and thinking longer arms make a bigger angle.

In the lab your child drags a protractor onto a vertex, reads three angles where the two scales disagree, estimates three angles before checking them, draws 135° and 70°, and finds two reflex angles from their inside angles.

practice.prompt: An acute angle's arm crosses 47 and 133 on a protractor. How big is it?
practice.hint: Acute angles are less than 90°. Which number fits?
practice.explain: Acute means less than 90°, so the angle is 47°. 133 is on the scale that starts at 180 on this arm.

practice.prompt: An arm crosses {a} on one scale of a protractor. What number does it cross on the other scale?
practice.hint: The two scales run opposite ways, so the two numbers always add up to 180.
practice.explain: 180 − {a} = {=180-a}. Only one of {a} and {=180-a} is the angle: use the scale that starts at 0 on your arm.

practice.prompt: Where does the protractor's centre mark go?
choices: At the end of an arm
On the edge of the paper
practice.hint: The vertex is where the two arms meet.
practice.explain: The centre mark goes on the vertex, and the 0 line lies along one arm.

practice.prompt: The inside angle is {a}°. How big is the reflex angle that goes the long way round?
practice.hint: A full turn is 360°. Take away the inside angle.
practice.explain: 360 − {a} = {=360-a}°. A reflex angle is more than 180°.

practice.prompt: You want to draw 135° from an arm pointing right. Where do you put the mark?
choices: At 135 on the scale that starts at 0 on the right
At 135 on the scale that starts at 0 on the left
practice.hint: Count up from the 0 that sits on your arm.
practice.explain: Use the scale whose 0 is on your arm. The other 135 mark would make a 45° angle.

pool.prompt: What unit do we use to measure the size of an angle?
pool.hint: Look at the small circle after the numbers in the lab.
pool.explain: Angles are measured in degrees, written with the ° sign, for example 90°.

pool.prompt: An obtuse angle's arm crosses 52 and 128. How big is it?
pool.explain: Obtuse means more than 90°, so the angle is 128°. 52 is on the other scale.

pool.prompt: Ben reads an angle as 150°, but it looks small and pointy. What has he most likely done?
pool.hint: A small, pointy angle is acute. What should it be less than?
pool.explain: An acute angle is less than 90°. 150° is on the other scale; the angle is 180 − 150 = 30°.

pool.prompt: Angle A has arms 10 cm long. Angle B has arms 3 cm long. Both measure 60°. Which is bigger?
choices: Neither, they are the same size
pool.hint: Does the length of the arms change the amount of turn between them?
pool.explain: Both are 60°. An angle measures the turn between the arms, not how long they are.

pool.prompt: An inside angle measures {a}°. How big is the reflex angle on the outside?
pool.hint: Inside and outside make a full turn of 360°.
pool.explain: 360 − {a} = {=360-a}°. The inside and outside angles together make a full turn.

pool.prompt: Which reading makes sense for an obtuse angle?
pool.hint: Obtuse angles are more than 90° and less than 180°.
pool.explain: 125° is between 90° and 180°. 55° is acute and 215° is reflex.

pool.prompt: Your bottom arm points left. Which scale do you read?
choices: The one with 0 on the left
The one with the biggest numbers
pool.hint: Which scale starts counting from your arm?
pool.explain: Count from the 0 that sits on your arm. No scale is always the right one.

pool.prompt: An arm crosses {a} on the outer scale. The angle is acute. How big is the angle?
pool.hint: The two numbers on the arm add to 180. An acute angle is the one less than 90°.
pool.explain: The two readings are {a} and {=180-a}. {a} is more than 90, so the acute angle is {=180-a}°.

pool.prompt: To draw an angle of 70°, what do you do after marking 70 on the right scale?
choices: Join the mark to the vertex with a ruler
Draw a curve to the mark
Move the protractor to the mark
pool.hint: An angle has two straight arms that meet at the vertex.
pool.explain: Join the mark to the vertex with a ruler to draw the second arm. The angle between the arms is 70°.
